knowledge_units.statement: Bias / offset updating is an established soft-sensor correction family in which the base predictor is left unchanged and an output correction is updated from observed prediction errors; reported variants include tuned/weighted and Bayesian bias estimators.
qualifiers: The selected evidence is concentrated in process-industry soft-sensor applications.

knowledge_units.statement: Bias correction has an explicit tracking-versus-variance/noise trade-off: in one analyzed statistical setting full bias updating removed bias but doubled variance, motivating weighted correction and gain tuning rather than unconditional one-for-one error injection.
qualifiers: The reported 100% variance increase is specific to the setting analyzed by Quelhas and Pinto and is not a universal numerical result.

knowledge_units.statement: Delayed, sporadic, or multirate quality measurements do not preclude external prediction correction; bias-updating methods have been formulated with explicit measurement delay and sampling-rate conditions, including Bayesian adaptation using sporadic laboratory measurements.
qualifiers: Correction design must account for the timing and frequency of the ground-truth quality measurements.

knowledge_units.statement: Prediction-error dynamics can be modeled in a separate residual model, such as ARMA, and the predicted future residual can be added to the output of a fixed base predictor.
qualifiers: Selected demonstrations include ethylene distillation simulation and an industrial reactive-distillation dataset.

knowledge_units.statement: Residual-prediction correction is conditional on the temporal structure of the residual: the selected ARMA-based work requires a stationary or transformable error process, held-out validation, and reports poor handling of serious disturbances or outliers.
qualifiers: These limitations are method-specific but illustrate that an auxiliary residual model can itself become invalid.

knowledge_units.statement: Kalman-filter/data-fusion correction can combine model predictions with measurements acquired at different rates to calibrate the soft-sensor output without changing the base predictor.
qualifiers: Reported performance depends on representing essential process dynamics and on appropriate filter tuning.

knowledge_units.statement: Correction-filter choice can materially change dynamic behavior; in one Kaibel dividing-wall-column study, EKF, UKF, and PF correction of the same soft sensor exhibited different oscillation and steady-state-offset behavior.
qualifiers: The evidence supports process-specific trade-offs, not a universal ranking of nonlinear filters.

knowledge_units.statement: A two-layer architecture can keep an offline/base prediction model separate from an adaptive calibration model that learns from prediction errors; the auxiliary calibration layer may be updated online while base-model parameters remain unchanged.
qualifiers: This satisfies the frozen-base-model boundary only if correction-layer parameters and base-model parameters are operationally and version-wise separated.

knowledge_units.statement: Output calibration is presented as simpler and lower-cost than base-model self-adjustment when operating conditions remain relatively stable, while simple bias correction may become insufficient under large working-condition changes.
qualifiers: A large operating-condition change is therefore an applicability boundary for simple correction, not evidence that retraining is automatically required.

knowledge_units.statement: The selected evidence supports at least five external correction families compatible with a frozen base predictor: simple/weighted bias correction, Bayesian/statistical bias estimation, residual time-series prediction, Kalman/state-data fusion, and a separately adaptive calibration model.
qualifiers: The families overlap conceptually; they are an engineering taxonomy for this Investigation rather than mutually exclusive formal categories.

knowledge_units.statement: Method selection depends on residual temporal structure, measurement noise and outliers, quality-measurement delay/rate, and magnitude of operating-condition change; the selected evidence does not support a process-independent correction gain, window size, filter, or universal numerical threshold.
qualifiers: Parameter values must be established and validated on the target process.

relations.description: Bias-update literature consistently treats delayed or sparse measured quality as a design condition for the correction mechanism rather than as a reason to modify the base model.
The existence of a bias-update method does not imply that full correction is desirable; weighting/tuning is needed to manage noise and variance.
The benefit of residual-prediction correction depends on whether the residual dynamics are sufficiently stable/modelable and on robustness to outliers or disturbances.
State/data-fusion filtering is a correction family, but filter structure and tuning have process-specific dynamic consequences.
A separate adaptive calibration layer can extend beyond simple bias correction when working conditions change, but it adds an adaptive model that must remain separated from the base predictor.
All four represented architectures correct the prediction outside the base predictor; they differ in how much structure is assigned to the correction state or correction model.

uncertainties.description: The selected literature is dominated by chemical/process soft-sensor applications, so transfer to other manufacturing sectors must be validated rather than assumed.

The studies use heterogeneous simulations, laboratory experiments, and specific industrial datasets, so the selected evidence does not provide a common benchmark from which to rank all correction families.

The RQ freezes the base prediction model but permits an external correction layer to adapt. Methods such as adaptive calibration models therefore remain in scope only under a strict architectural separation between base-model and correction-layer parameters.
No selected evidence establishes process-independent numerical settings for correction gain, residual-model order, window length, Kalman tuning, or escalation thresholds.
No target-process dataset was supplied in this Investigation, so the evidence can support method families and selection conditions but not numerical tuning or process-specific performance claims.
